newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Dutch ABN AMRO Bank eyes Colombia, Peru.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ABN AMRO Bank eyes Colombia, Peru.

text.p: Dutch ABN AMRO Bank said it plans to increase its presence in Latin America by entering Colombia and, at a later stage, Peru.

"We intend to enter Colombia and, at a later stage, Peru," said M.J. Drabbe, member of ABN AMRO Bank's Managing Board, in a presentation speech to international financial press in the bank's Brazil head office in Sao Paulo.

"We also intend to expand our current base in Argentina and Venezuela. This means that for now, with the exception of Bolivia and the Central American countries, we expect to cover the whole continent in the not-too-distant future," he said.

ABN AMRO Bank has 124 branches in 12 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean. In 1995, profits derived from South and Central America, which account for eight percent of the group's pre-tax profits, increased 165 percent against the previous year, the bank said.
Drabbe said in his speech ABN AMRO is confident on Latin America because the region, "only trailing Asia, is expected to show the strongest GDP growth through 2005."

Despite expectations that South East Asia as a region will remain the main recipient of foreign capital flows to emerging markets, ABN AMRO Bank said flows to Latin America should increase in absolute terms.

"Provided that capital flows will continue to grow at the same rate as in 1990-1995 period, a total of $200 billion will enter the region in the next five years," Drabbe said, adding that Brazil and Argentina will witness the strongest inflows.
The ABN AMRO Bank official also said the bank wants to be a leading regional network bank in Latin America.
